method: Read every AC table in sdlc/06.analysis/03.acceptance-criteria/{08,09,10,46,47,48,49}; read all candidate sources; ran the 4 qc suites (32/32 pass); then probed the functions with objects produced by the product's OWN domain models (createRole, createWorker, savePolicy, sdlc-config unified config) rather than the synthetic shapes used by the tests. Grading rule: an AC is PASS only if the behaviour holds for the product's real domain objects AND a test asserts it. An AC is demoted when the product's existing durable vocabulary contradicts the value being recorded (e.g. an 'expired' risk event that evidence_risk's CHECK rejects). Absence of any store/wiring is reported once as a cluster-level defect, not multiplied into every AC.

acs.gap: The bar is compared by string identity, but the product's role model defines bar items as objects ({evidence_kind, min_basis}) and matches them by kind. Probe with createRole({bar:[{evidence_kind:'diff',min_basis:'full'},...]}) and carries ['diff','test_log'] returns BLOCKED HANDOFF_INCOMPLETE with missing=[{evidence_kind:'diff',...},{evidence_kind:'test_log',...}]. The happy path is therefore unreachable for any role built by US-IAM-02; the test only passes because it invents a string-array bar that no product code produces.

impl: eso/control-plane/src/flow.mjs:160 — "... Missing required evidence: ${missing.join(', ')} (bar of role '${to}')"
acs.gap: Blocking works for the string-bar shape the test invents. With a real role bar the 'missing items' list contains objects and the human-readable message degenerates to '[object Object]' (flow.mjs:160 joins objects), so 'nêu thiếu mục nào' is not met for product data. It also blocks every handover, which makes the refusal assert vacuously true.
Shape-independent; the returned event carries unconstrained:true and the test asserts it. (Not persisted anywhere — see cluster defect C-04.)
Throws before any mutation (validateAndCreateFlow is pure), so 0 changes holds.
'1 flow' is only guaranteed across the caller-supplied existingFlows array (no flow store exists).
Both direct self-cycle and A→B→A are asserted. Cycle detection also merges other flows of the same project, which is stricter than the AC but consistent with it.

impl: eso/control-plane/src/debt.mjs:90 — "const acceptEvent = {" (fields: event, risk_id, by, due, role, timestamp)
acs.gap: AC §4 requires the event to record by · due · reason; no `reason` field exists — probe: acceptHasReason=false. The event also lives only in a caller-passed array; nothing writes it to evidence_risk (see cluster defect C-04).

Refusal works, but the AC's error identifier is ACCEPT_WITHOUT_DUE (absent from the whole repo), and the sibling AC 46/AC-IAM-08-02 demands ACCEPT_NO_DUE for the same action — the SoT contradicts itself. The test dodges the conflict with a permissive OR that pins neither contract.

Status recalculates and the event is emitted in memory, but the product's only risk store cannot hold it: evidence_risk.CHECK excludes 'expired' and has no due column, so 'ghi sự kiện expired' is unrepresentable end-to-end.
proof: eso/evidence/src/schema.mjs:108 — "event TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event IN ('open','opened','accept','accepted','mitigate','mitigated','close','closed','reopen','reopened')),"

acs.gap: RBAC is opt-in: with the default allowedKindsForRole=null the permission check is skipped entirely, and the allowed kinds are injected by the caller rather than derived from the role model (role.mjs capabilities/bar). The AC's identifier ACCEPT_FORBIDDEN is not implemented anywhere; the test asserts the invented FORBIDDEN_ACCEPT.
Guard only fires on status==='accepted'; a 'closed' risk can be re-accepted (probe: acceptClosedRisk='accepted'), which the AC's 'risk open' precondition implies should not happen. Minor.
Strict '>' makes the due instant inclusive.

impl: eso/control-plane/src/config-mgr.mjs:38 — "const affected_artefacts = artefacts.filter((a) => a.project === project).map((a) => a.id);"
acs.gap: Preview reads fields that do not exist on the product's unified config ({version, groups:{sdlc,team,tools,project}}, roles keyed by name). Probe with a real config returns users=[] and overrides=[] — i.e. 'nobody uses it, nobody overrides it' — while affected_artefacts lists every project artefact regardless of the change. The test passes only because it invents currentConfig.roles/custom_overrides.

impl: eso/control-plane/src/config-mgr.mjs:85 — "'PREVIEW_HASH_MISMATCH: Configuration changes must be previewed prior to save; ...'"
acs.gap: Save without a matching preview is refused (correct behaviour, hash-bound), but the AC's error is PREVIEW_REQUIRED, which appears nowhere in the repo; the test asserts the code the implementation invented.

Postcondition 'sự kiện revert' is missing: the function returns config+marked artefacts only, no revert event, and never touches the durable config_event table that already exists for this action. `currentConfig` is accepted and unused, the window's upper bound [lưu, revert] is never checked, and the caller must move the version pointer itself.
proof: eso/evidence/src/schema.mjs:117 — "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS config_event (" (kind CHECK 'save','revert') — never written by this path
eso/control-plane/src/config-mgr.mjs:118 — "export function revertConfigChange({" (currentConfig param, unused in body)

acs.gap: Only the mutation path is guarded, and the guard is defeated by any config object without a `project` key (probe: save for project-B against {version:1} succeeds). Reading is not isolated at all: previewing project-B with project-A's config returns A's base_version/users/overrides (probe crossTenantPreview). AC requires 'không thấy' and error OUT_OF_SCOPE; neither exists.
Hash is recomputed from {project, baseVersion, pendingChange}; exact match saves and bumps version. Not persisted (see C-04).

No preset upgrade exists anywhere: control-plane only computes an impact array in preview (the string 'upgrade' is a label). The AC requires 'nâng đủ 50; 50 project' — a state change — but the test asserts only the length of the list it was handed. The filter also counts projects already on the same preset as needing an 'upgrade'.
proof: eso/control-plane/src/index.mjs:23 — "export {" (only scope-guard/flow/debt/config-mgr symbols are re-exported; no upgrade function exists)
MISSING: eso/control-plane/src/{config-mgr,flow,debt}.mjs — no apply/upgrade function for preset_id

acs.gap: 'Lưu due' is only a returned field: the product's risk table has no due column at all, so an acceptance with an expiry cannot be stored and later read by anyone (see C-04).
Identifier matches this AC (it conflicts with AC-IAM-05-02, see that entry); the assertion is loose but the thrown code is ACCEPT_NO_DUE.
Status flips to expired on read and an event is emitted, but 'expired' is not an allowed evidence_risk event, so the record the AC demands ('có ghi') cannot survive a read.
proof: eso/evidence/src/schema.mjs:108 — "event TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event IN ('open','opened','accept','accepted','mitigate','mitigated','close','closed','reopen','reopened')),"

acs.gap: Inclusive boundary asserted at exactly `due`.

Offset-bearing strings ('+07:00') are compared in UTC as required. Residual risk: a timezone-LESS string ('2026-11-04T12:00:00') would be parsed as machine-local; no test covers it, but the accept path normalises to toISOString() so the stored value is safe.

Impact is computed from an invented policy shape. The domain's policy is {policy_id, attribute} (single string), so against saved policies the preview reports 0 affected (probe impactOnRealPolicies.affected_count=0) and even if a policy matched, affected_policies would be [undefined] because policies use policy_id, not id/name. The test supplies `uses:[...]` objects that no product code can produce.

Agent mutation is refused, but via a hard-coded name allowlist rather than the role/verb model (CLOSED_VERBS already has 'configure'), and the AC's identifier POLICY_FORBIDDEN is not implemented anywhere. The test asserts the invented FORBIDDEN_MUTATION.

The in-use guard never fires for real policies: probe with a saved policy {policy_id:'pol-1', attribute:'project'} returns success:true for delete — exactly the orphaned-policy state the AC forbids ('0 policy mồ côi'). The test passes on the invented `uses` field.

This is a caller-supplied equality check, not a compare-and-set: two operators that both read version 1 both pass and both 'win' (nothing arbitrates). The ED7 scenario — simultaneous save, one winner — is not representable; the test only replays a stale number sequentially.

Wrong identifier (AC requires ATTRIBUTE_IN_USE), and the migration branch is a boolean flag that migrates nothing: probe renames 'project'→'geo' with hasMigrationPlan:true while the policy still says attribute:'project' — the exact orphan the AC forbids, blessed by the passing test.

Roles are matched by `id` and customization by a `customized` flag — neither exists on a real role ({project,name,version,capabilities,scope,bar,status,policies}). Probe: a project holding a real 'lead' role ends with 8 roles, two 'lead' entries, skipped=[] — the hand-edited role is duplicated, not preserved.
proof: eso/iam/src/role.mjs:83 — "name," (role identity is name; no id/customized in the returned role)

impl: eso/core/src/team-tool-cfg.mjs:81 — "const assignedWorkers = workers.filter((w) => w.role_id === roleId && w.state !== 'retired');"
acs.gap: Workers are keyed by `role_id`, but the product's worker carries `role_name`. Probe with createWorker({role:'build',state:'active'}): deleteTeamRole returns success:true — an in-use role is deleted. The guard is dead on real objects; the test invents {role_id:'build'}.

Diff renders and does not apply, but it is keyed on the same invented `id`/`customized`: against real roles every preset role reads as 'added' and the user's real roles read as 'removed' (a diff that proposes deleting hand-made roles). The 'preset mới hơn' branch (`modified`, line 121) is untested; and even if shown, applyTeamPreset silently ignores non-customized existing roles (line 39-44) — diff and apply disagree.
With 0 existing roles the shape mismatch is irrelevant; 7 preset roles are installed and skipped is empty.

The orphan warning is keyed on `w.role_id`; a real worker ({role_name:'deprecated-role'}) yields missing_roles=[] — the missing role is silently not reported (probe). No auto-reassignment does happen, but the AC's 'báo vai thiếu' half is dead for product data.
'Lưu' is a returned literal object: declareToolConfig has no store and no caller, so the config exists only in the test's local variable. Status is correct.

With an injected probe that throws, the marking is correct. But the probe is injected by the caller, and with no probe the function reports 'connected' without testing anything (probe verifyNoProbe='connected') — precisely the 'returns ok without acting' case; AC §2 forbids treating unverified as 'has tool'.

Nothing is switched: `source: pack.source` is a tautological self-assignment, no local pack is produced (probe switchLocalPacks=0), and `current_source` merely echoes the argument. The test asserts the old source is unchanged — trivially true because the function mutates nothing. '2 nguồn phân biệt được' is not implemented.

impl: eso/core/src/team-tool-cfg.mjs:190 — "const existingIndex = existingConnections.findIndex((c) => c.tool_id === toolId && c.project === project);"
acs.gap: Single record updated in place. The AC's `verified_at` is named `last_checked_at` and its freshness is not asserted (both runs can share a millisecond), but the no-duplication core is proven.

The verbatim round-trip is a shallow copy compared against the same in-memory input — no write and no read-back, so 'đọc lại khớp từng ký tự' is not demonstrated; the assertion would hold for any echo function.

top_defects.proof: eso/control-plane/src/flow.mjs:156 — "const missing = bar.filter((req) => !carriedSet.has(req));" vs eso/iam/src/role.mjs:74 — "if (!item.evidence_kind || !item.min_basis) {"; probe cluster-c-probe2.mjs blocks a complete handover with missing=[{evidence_kind:'diff',...}]

top_defects.proof: eso/control-plane/src/config-mgr.mjs:219 — "if (Array.isArray(p.attributes_used)) ..." vs eso/iam/src/policy.mjs:47 — "const attribute = policy.attribute;"; probe: deleting a real in-use attribute returns success:true (0 orphans prevented)

top_defects.proof: eso/core/src/team-tool-cfg.mjs:81 — "workers.filter((w) => w.role_id === roleId ...)" vs eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:72 — "role_name: assignedRole,"; probe: deleting a role held by an active real worker succeeds; preset duplicates an existing real role (8 roles, skipped [])

top_defects.proof: eso/evidence/src/schema.mjs:108 — "event TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event IN ('open','opened','accept','accepted',...))" (no 'expired'); eso/control-plane/src/debt.mjs is used only by qc tests — no adapter writes these events

top_defects.title: Preview/verify/switch return computed shapes without acting; two ACs have no apply path at all
top_defects.proof: eso/core/src/team-tool-cfg.mjs:223 — "source: pack.source," (tautology, 0 local packs) and :172 "let status = 'connected';" (no probe ⇒ success); eso/control-plane/src/config-mgr.mjs:48 — "action: 'upgrade'," with no upgrade function in eso/control-plane/src/index.mjs

contract_defects: Error identifiers demanded by the ACs do not exist anywhere in the repo: PREVIEW_REQUIRED, ACCEPT_WITHOUT_DUE, ACCEPT_FORBIDDEN, POLICY_FORBIDDEN, and OUT_OF_SCOPE for tenant isolation; the tests assert the implemented substitutes (PREVIEW_HASH_MISMATCH, ACCEPT_NO_DUE, FORBIDDEN_ACCEPT, FORBIDDEN_MUTATION, TENANT_VIOLATION).

AC-IAM-05-02 requires ACCEPT_WITHOUT_DUE while AC-IAM-08-02 requires ACCEPT_NO_DUE for the same trigger — the SoT contradicts itself; qc/eso-cp-debt.test.mjs:47 hides the conflict behind an OR that pins neither.
AC-IAM-06-04 'không thấy' is unimplemented: previewConfigChange has no tenant notion; probing project-B with project-A's config returns A's base_version/users/overrides.

ac3_test_files.assessment: No AC fails solely because its named file is absent — every AC has an equivalent test — but none of the 22 names in the AC tables exist, so the AC↔test traceability the SoT declares is fictional.

notes: All 32 tests in the 4 equivalent suites pass; they pass because they construct the objects the implementation expects (string bars, `uses` arrays, `role_id` workers) rather than objects built by eso/iam or eso/knowledge — the green suite is the defect's camouflage.

No product wiring exists for any function in this cluster: outside qc/*.test.mjs the only reference is each domain's index.mjs re-export (verified by repo-wide grep), so 'saved', 'recorded' and 'one board record' are all return values.

Self-reported comments/artifacts/slp/audit/*.json were not used; no audit JSON exists for these seven tickets, so no 100/100 claim was contradicted — the findings stand on code and probes under /tmp/eso-dd/.
